report.currency: ZAR (South African rand); tables in R millions with ~USD equivalents at USD/ZAR 17.55
report.verdict: A buyback-flattered print: HEPS +7% to 79c (~4.5 USc) masks headline earnings -2% to R757m (~$43m), income -2% to R5.43bn (~$309m) and adj. EBITDA -4% to R1.65bn (~$94m) as slot-machine GGR keeps leaking to online casino-style betting and the Gold Reef City strike cost ~R59m (~$3.4m). The balance sheet is the good news — net debt -12% YoY to R5.99bn (~$341m), 1.81x covenant leverage hits the <1.8x target — and online betting (NGR +43%, 26% margin) is finally real, but management's warning that October and November were "particularly tough" tells you H2 will not rescue the year.
summary: **Soft, and softer than the headline suggests.** Six months to 30 Sept 2026 (H1 FY27; FYE 31 March; JSE: TSG): total income -2% to R5.43bn (~$309m), adj. EBITDA -4% to R1.65bn (~$94m) at a 30.3% margin (-60bp YoY, -110bp vs H2 FY26's 31.4%). There is no meaningful sell-side consensus for this small cap; domestic press characterised the result as poor in a tough market, with HEPS growth only possible because of buybacks (News24, quoting JustOne Lap's Simon Brown).

**HEPS +7% to 79c (~4.5 USc) is a denominator story.** Headline earnings fell 2% to R757m (~$43m) and IFRS attributable profit fell 7% to R630m (~$36m); the weighted share count dropped 7.6% to 961m after 62m shares were cancelled in FY26 and a further 10m (R67m/~$3.8m at R6.70) in H1 FY27. Basic/diluted IFRS EPS was 66c (~3.8 USc) vs 65c.

**R70m (~$4.0m) of 'specific events' at EBITDA level, R67m at headline level.** Management's own bridge: industrial action/intimidation at Gold Reef City -R43m, once-off labour cost -R16m, lower dividends received -R8m (City Lodge stake sold), historical VAT/interest -R3m; plus -R11m at headline level from the casino sale. Adding the R70m back gives ~R1.72bn (~$98m), i.e. flat YoY (our estimate) — the underlying business is treading water, not growing.

**The division driving the decline is Casinos & Hotels (73% of income, 86% of EBITDA).** Divisional income -3% to R3.99bn (~$227m), adj. EBITDA -7% to R1.41bn (~$80m), margin -150bp to 35.4%. Management presents it as -6% 'excluding the Theme Park, which was down 37%'. The root cause is slot-machine win: group net gaming win -3.4% to R4.45bn (~$253m) while rooms revenue grew 11% to R312m (~$18m) and F&B was flat at R331m (~$19m).

**Gauteng is where it hurt.** Gauteng income -3% to R2.33bn (~$133m), EBITDA -10% to R835m (~$48m), margin -270bp to 35.9%. The THORN-union strike at Gold Reef City Casino & Theme Park (from late April 2026, into a second month by late May; theme park closed, casino partially affected) cost an estimated R43m directly plus R16m once-off labour; even adding both back, Gauteng EBITDA is still ~-3% (estimate). The GRC casino-floor upgrade completed in November 2026; the 5D cinema lands ~June 2027.

**Impairments R158m (~$9m), of which R150m (~$8.5m) is the Gold Reef City casino licence** (recoverable amount R2.4bn/~$137m) — the second consecutive GRC write-down after R144m at March 2026. Sensitivity disclosure: a 1pp higher discount rate would trigger a further R273m (~$16m) GRC impairment; a 1pp lower trading assumption, R174m. Blackrock goodwill took another R10m (R73m in FY26).

**KwaZulu-Natal (Suncoast) was the only region that grew**: income +1.6% to R1.08bn (~$62m), EBITDA +3.7% to R423m (~$24m), margin +80bp to 39.0% — a recovery after FY26's -9% EBITDA. Western Cape was the worst: income -8% to R258m (~$15m), EBITDA -17% to R81m (~$4.6m), margin -360bp.

**Online betting (playTSOGO, bet.co.za) is now a genuine contributor**: NGR +43% to R193m (~$11m), adj. EBITDA R50m (~$2.8m) at a 26% margin vs R13m at 10%; the business has been profitable every month since August 2025 and now runs ~R8m/month. Sequentially, though, NGR grew only +8% vs the derived H2 FY26 R178m (~$10m) after +32% the prior half — momentum has decelerated, and no handle, actives, ARPU or marketing data are disclosed.

**LPMs (VSlots) held flat in a shrinking market**: income R989m (~$56m, -0.4%), EBITDA R282m (~$16m, -0.4%), margin steady at 28.5%, 17.1% of group EBITDA (16.5%). Peer Sun Slots' EBITDA fell 8.1% in H1 CY26, so Tsogo's route business is outperforming. Growth hinges on the NGB finally adjusting the R5 max bet / R500 max payout unchanged since 1996 — a new National Gambling Board was appointed in October 2026, the first in over a decade.

**No formal earnings guidance; the quantified guideposts moved as follows.** FY27 capex trimmed to ~R1.1bn (~$63m) from R1.2bn in May; the medium-term leverage target (<1.8x) is 'effectively achieved' at 1.81x; the Somerset West relocation timeline compressed to 'approximately a year and a half' from 'approximately two years'; and the qualitative outlook deteriorated — 'October and November have been particularly tough trading months'.

**Balance sheet: the genuine positive.** Net debt (NIBD & guarantees) -R810m YoY and -R495m since March to R5.99bn (~$341m); covenant leverage 1.81x vs 1.92x (Mar-26) and 2.01x (Sep-25), covenant <3.0x. Net finance costs (ex-IFRS 16) -14% to R253m (~$14m), though SARB's +50bp of hikes (April and September 2026) partly offset. R4.45bn (~$254m) of calendar-2027 maturities (R500m Feb, R1.0bn May, R900m Aug, plus R650m and R1.5bn RCFs) are 'in advanced stages' of refinancing; current liabilities now exceed current assets (R4.49bn vs R1.02bn) pending that refinancing.

**Cash generation intact.** Cash generated from operations R1.68bn (~$96m), flat YoY; capex R344m (~$20m), also flat; our estimated pre-dividend free cash flow ~R790m (~$45m) vs ~R750m. Net cash from operating activities (Tsogo's definition, after interest, tax and dividends) rose 10% to R824m (~$47m). R358m (~$20m) was returned to shareholders (R291m dividends + R67m buybacks); a further 4.7m shares (R32m/~$1.8m) were bought at R6.70 post period, taking shares in issue to 965.6m.

**Interim dividend held at 15c (~0.9 USc), R145m (~$8.3m) aggregate**, payable 21 Dec 2026 (LDT 14 Dec). Controlling shareholder HCI received R157m (~$8.9m) of dividends in the half and its indirect stake has crept to 54% (50% a year ago) as buybacks shrink the register.

**Portfolio pruning and asset sales continue**: the two smallest casinos were sold (R97m proceeds; 13 casinos now vs 15), vacant land is being sold for R48m (~$2.7m) net and R65m (~$3.7m) of listed shares are held for sale — '>R100m' of further realisations earmarked for debt/buybacks. Group capital commitments stand at R1bn (~$57m) for the next 12 months.

**Somerset West is the growth project — and a legal fight.** The Caledon licence relocation to the Helderberg (~R1.29bn/~$74m estimated cost, per the Nov-25 booklet) has regulatory approval, but the sole metropole operator (~82% Western Cape casino market share, i.e. Sun International's GrandWest, in which Tsogo itself holds a 20% FVOCI stake valued at R511m) has taken the decision on High Court review; hearing April 2027. Tsogo is proceeding regardless.

**Regulatory overhang is dense**: proposed ban on dedicated casino smoking areas; the National Gambling Amendment Bill (costly system requirements) held over by Parliament; unresolved online-betting taxation and casinos' inability to offer products online; provincial attempts to raise casino taxes while online 'betting' operators offering casino-style slots pay less; Eastern Cape LPM route licence expires March 2027 and goes to formal rebid.

**Peer read-through is unflattering.** Sun International (six months to June 2026) grew land-based casino income +1.5% to R3.42bn (~$195m) and SunBet online income +35% to R1.18bn (~$67m) — Tsogo's casinos shrank 3% and its online business is roughly one-sixth of SunBet's scale. The bear case is share loss in both channels; the bull case is that Tsogo's cash yield and deleveraging do not require growth.

**Share price**: +~1% by late afternoon on results day (News24); the stock is -8% YTD vs Sun International +22% and Southern Sun +8%, trading at roughly R7 (~$0.40) — ~4.5x trailing HEPS of 158c and a ~6.4% dividend yield on 45c. Exact close on 25 Nov not verified.

**What management emphasises vs buries**: the booklet leads with 'HEPS up 7%' and debt reduction, and quotes casino EBITDA 'excluding the Theme Park'; the slots decline, the Oct/Nov trading warning, the second GRC impairment and its R273m sensitivity sit in the body. There is still no disclosure of hotel occupancy/ADR, online actives/handle or marketing spend, and no public results call.

**Thesis read-through**: a cheap, cash-generative, now-deleveraged land-based operator with a structural slot problem and a sub-scale but profitable online hedge. The equity case rests on capital returns (dividends + buybacks ~R0.9bn/yr), online optionality and regulatory relief (LPM limits, online rights for casinos), not on a land-based recovery — and the H2 trading warning plus 2027 refinancing at higher rates are the near-term swing factors.

segments.name: Casinos & Hotels (Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Western Cape, Other casinos)
segments.headline: Slot-win erosion plus the Gold Reef City strike drove income -3% to R3.99bn (~$227m) and EBITDA -7% to R1.41bn (~$80m); KZN grew, Gauteng and the Western Cape fell hard, and management says Oct/Nov got worse.
narrative: The precinct business, which is 73% of group income and 86% of adjusted EBITDA, delivered income of R3.99bn (~$227m), down 2.7% year on year and 2.4% on the preceding half, with adjusted EBITDA of R1.41bn (~$80m), down 6.9% year on year and 6.7% half on half, so the margin slipped 150bp to 35.4% and the sequential picture (37.0% in H2 FY26) shows the compression is accelerating rather than lapping a weak base. Management's preferred framing is that divisional EBITDA fell 6% 'excluding the Theme Park, which was down 37%'; on our arithmetic the Theme Park went from 'more than R50m' (~$2.8m) of EBITDA a year ago to roughly R32m (~$1.8m), so the exclusion is worth about a point. The stated driver is unchanged from the last three reporting periods — the decline in revenue generated by slot machines — and the impairment note is more candid than the commentary, attributing the underperformance of gaming win to pressured discretionary spend together with casino-styled online betting games continuing to grow to significant levels. Group net gaming win fell 3.4% to R4.45bn (~$253m), and because revenue from contracts with customers in this division actually grew 4.7% to R827m (~$47m) — rooms +11.4% to R312m (~$18m), F&B +2.3% to R315m (~$18m), other revenue flat at R200m — the implied gaming-and-other-income line fell about 4.5% to ~R3.16bn (~$180m), which is the number that matters for the margin. Divisional gaming levies and VAT fell in line with win (-4.4% to R659m/~$38m, 16.5% of income) and employee costs were held at R756m (~$43m, -0.9%), so the operating leverage is coming almost entirely through the gaming-win line.

Gauteng, at 58% of divisional income, carried the damage: income fell 3.0% to R2.33bn (~$133m) and EBITDA fell 9.7% to R835m (~$48m), a 270bp margin decline to 35.9%, with EBITDA also down 7.6% on the preceding half. The group's bridge attributes R43m (~$2.5m) of EBITDA to the direct impact of industrial action and intimidation at Gold Reef City Casino and Theme Park and a further R16m (~$0.9m) to a once-off labour-related cost; the THORN-affiliated strike began in late April 2026, closed the theme park and partially disrupted the casino, and was still running into its second month by late May on a dispute between a 4% offer and a 12% demand. Even adding both items back, Gauteng EBITDA would still have been down roughly 3% (our estimate), consistent with the underlying slot trend at Montecasino and Silverstar, neither of which is disclosed separately. Management says recovery at Gold Reef City 'is difficult'; the casino gaming-floor upgrade was completed in November 2026 and a redeveloped 5D cinema at the Theme Park should follow by about June 2027. The accounting tells the same story: the Gold Reef City licence was impaired by a further R150m (~$8.5m), following R144m at March 2026, to a recoverable amount of R2.4bn (~$137m), and the sensitivity table shows a 1pp rise in the discount rate would cost another R273m (~$16m), a 1pp cut to trading assumptions R174m (~$10m). Pre-tax discount rates were actually lowered 40–60bp across the CGUs (Montecasino, Suncoast and Gold Reef City all to 16.4%) on the back of the sovereign upgrade, so the impairment was taken despite a valuation tailwind.

KwaZulu-Natal, essentially Suncoast plus Golden Horse and Blackrock, was the only region to grow: income rose 1.6% to R1.08bn (~$62m) and EBITDA 3.7% to R423m (~$24m), lifting the margin 80bp to 39.0%, the highest in the portfolio, with income also 2.2% higher than the preceding half. That is a creditable reversal after FY26, when KZN EBITDA fell 9% and management described the performance as 'under pressure'; it is also where gaming levies rose (R221m vs R217m) in step with win, implying genuine volume rather than cost cutting. Blackrock remains the weak link — its goodwill took another R10m impairment (recoverable amount R127m) after R73m in FY26 — but at a regional level KZN is now the stabiliser in the land-based book.

The Western Cape was the worst performer on every line: income fell 7.9% to R258m (~$15m), EBITDA 17.3% to R81m (~$4.6m), and the margin collapsed 360bp to 31.4% (and 620bp against the seasonally stronger H2 FY26, when Cape summer trading produced R114m). The Caledon, already flagged for double-digit declines and a R40m goodwill write-off at March, is the drag, and the group's response is to relocate that licence to the Helderberg (Somerset West/Strand) at an estimated ~R1.29bn (~$74m) over what is now 'approximately a year and a half'. The regulator has approved it, but the sole casino operator in the Cape Town metropole — holding ~82% of Western Cape casino market share, i.e. GrandWest, in which Tsogo itself retains a 20% FVOCI stake carried at R511m (~$29m) — has instituted High Court proceedings to review the approval and interdict implementation, with the hearing set for April 2027. Tsogo says it remains committed and is already spending on the site, so the FY27 capex envelope of ~R1.1bn (~$63m) and the FY28 commitment carry litigation risk that the booklet acknowledges but does not quantify. Other casinos (Emerald, Hemingway's, Goldfields, Mykonos, Garden Route and the rest) saw income fall 9.8% to R322m (~$18m) and EBITDA 14.3% to R72m (~$4.1m), partly because the two smallest casinos were sold during the period (R97m proceeds; FY26 EBITDA contribution R11m), taking the estate from 15 to 13 casinos; Hemingway's took a R1m PPE impairment.

On the hotel side the booklet offers no occupancy, ADR or RevPAR, only that the portfolio 'produced solid growth in rooms revenue' (+11.4% at group level to R312m) and that the Pivot hotel fifth-floor upgrade was among the period's projects; the F&B line was flat. The IT programme — one-card across the largest casinos (implemented), gaming-system upgrades, single sign-on, a hotel booking engine, the Tsogo Sun Rewards app, AI in certain processes and a resort wallet — is where management is directing the non-gaming capex, and divisional additions to non-current assets were R268m (~$15m) versus R284m. The most important sentence in the segment commentary is the trading update: 'subsequent to this period, October and November have been particularly tough trading months'. H2 is normally the slightly stronger half (H2 FY26 divisional income R4.09bn, EBITDA R1.51bn), so a continuation of a -3% income / -7% EBITDA run-rate would put FY27 divisional EBITDA in the ~R2.8bn (~$160m) area versus R3.03bn in FY26; the GRC refurbishment and the festive season are the only identified offsets.

Two things management does not say loudly deserve note. First, the group's casinos pay levies and VAT of 16.5% of divisional income while complaining that online 'betting' operators offering casino-style slots are taxed significantly less and that provincial authorities are attempting to tax casinos higher — the regulatory arbitrage against which Tsogo's land-based estate is losing share is not closing. Second, the proposed tobacco legislation banning dedicated smoking areas in casinos remains live; the booklet merely says it is being 'monitored', but for a slot-led estate this is the single largest unpriced regulatory risk.

segments.name: Limited Payout Machines (VSlots)
segments.headline: Flat income (R989m/~$56m) and EBITDA (R282m/~$16m) at a steady 28.5% margin — resilient against a peer whose LPM EBITDA fell 8% — but growth is hostage to 1996-era bet limits.
narrative: The route business produced income of R989m (~$56m), down 0.4% year on year and 0.8% on the preceding half, and adjusted EBITDA of R282m (~$16m), down 0.4% year on year but up 1.1% half on half, holding the margin at 28.5% (28.0% in H2 FY26). Management describes this as performing 'relatively well' in a tough market and highlights that LPMs now contribute 17.1% of group EBITDA against 16.5% a year ago — which is partly a function of the casinos shrinking faster. The deceleration is nonetheless clear: this division grew income 4% and EBITDA 5% in H1 FY26 and 3%/3% in FY26, and has now stalled. The cost structure is stable — gaming levies and VAT of R232m (~$13m) take 23.5% of income, materially above the 16.5% levied on casinos, and employee costs rose 4% to R47m (~$2.7m) — so the flat EBITDA reflects flat machine win rather than any cost action.

Against Sun International's Sun Slots, which reported income -0.4% to R698m (~$40m) and EBITDA -8.1% to R148m (~$8.4m) for the six months to June 2026 citing protests and weak Western Cape execution, Tsogo's VSlots has defended margin considerably better, and at R989m of half-year income it is the larger of the two route operators by some distance. We would nonetheless not read 'flat' as a floor: the division sells the same slot product that is losing share to online casino-style betting in the casino estate, with the one difference that its venues are convenience-led (taverns, bingo-adjacent sites) where the online substitution is slower.

The upside case is regulatory and has been for a decade. The R5 maximum bet and R500 maximum payout have been unchanged since 1996, and the group has been lobbying the National Gambling Board and the DTIC for an inflationary adjustment that would mechanically lift win per machine. A new National Gambling Board was appointed in October 2026 — the first in over ten years — which at least creates a decision-maker; the second-phase LPM roll-outs in KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga and North West are also awaiting NGB approval. On the risk side, the Eastern Cape route-operator licence expires in March 2027 and goes to a formal bidding process, a near-term event that management mentioned in May but does not repeat in this booklet.

Capital allocation reflects the wait-and-see stance: additions to non-current assets fell 44% to R50m (~$2.8m) from R89m, and the division is being run for cash. For modelling purposes we assume FY27 LPM EBITDA of ~R560m (~$32m), flat on FY26's R562m, with the bet-limit adjustment treated as unmodelled optionality worth, on our rough estimate, a high-single-digit uplift to divisional win if and when granted.

New National Gambling Board appointed October 2026, first in over ten years; second-phase roll-outs in KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga and North West await NGB approval.
Eastern Cape route-operator licence expires March 2027 and goes to formal bidding; mentioned in May but not repeated in this booklet.

blocks.heading: Capex and forecast
blocks.takeaway: Additions to non-current assets fell 44% to R50m (~$2.8m) from R89m; we assume FY27 LPM EBITDA ~R560m (~$32m), flat on R562m.
points: Division is being run for cash on a wait-and-see stance.
Bet-limit adjustment treated as unmodelled optionality worth, on our rough estimate, a high-single-digit uplift to divisional win if granted.

segments.name: Other gaming & betting (online betting — playTSOGO & bet.co.za; Galaxy Bingo; HHR associates)
segments.headline: Online NGR +43% to R193m (~$11m) with EBITDA R50m (~$2.8m) at 26% lifted segment EBITDA +52% to R73m, but sequential online growth slowed to +8%, bingo is shrinking ~20%, and the disclosure is too thin to judge customer economics.
narrative: The segment reported income of R429m (~$24m), down 1.8% year on year and 8.1% on the preceding half, but adjusted EBITDA of R73m (~$4.2m), up 52% year on year and 35% half on half, taking the margin to 17.0% from 11.0%. Everything positive in that mix is online. The online betting business — previously loss-making, turned around from August 2025 — generated gross gaming revenue net of bonusing of R193m (~$11m), up 43% from R135m (the prior booklet said R136m; we use the company's current comparative), and adjusted EBITDA of R50m (~$2.8m) at a 26% margin, against R13m at 10% a year earlier. Against our derived H2 FY26 figures (FY26 NGR R313m less H1 R135m, i.e. R178m/~$10m; EBITDA R50m less R13m, i.e. R37m), the half-on-half growth was +8% in NGR and +35% in EBITDA, with margin up 510bp. The monthly EBITDA run-rate is therefore about R8.3m, versus the 'more than R7m per month' management cited for August–October 2025.

The numbers merit two sceptical observations. First, the sequential deceleration from +32% (H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26) to +8% (H1 FY27 vs H2 FY26) is notable for a business that a year ago said it would 'grow more aggressively', 'may need to sacrifice a portion of its profits generated in the short term', and was 'exploring the launch of a new platform by the end of the 2026 financial year'; the FY27 language has softened to 'development of systems and the product portfolio, and improvement of customer experience'. A 26% EBITDA margin at R193m of half-year NGR implies marketing intensity well below what scaled South African operators spend, and segment employee costs rising 23% to R106m (~$6.0m) — the new online CEO and senior team who joined around February 2026 — is the only visible investment line. Second, scale: Sun International's SunBet generated R1.18bn (~$67m) of online income in the six months to June 2026, growing 35%, so Tsogo's online business is roughly one-sixth the size of its nearest listed peer and far smaller than the private bookmaker leaders; +43% off this base does not change the competitive picture. The booklet provides no handle, actives, ARPU, sportsbook-versus-casino mix, deposit or marketing data — all n/a — so there is no way to assess cohort quality or structural margin, and we treat the division's valuation contribution as option value rather than a modellable growth line.

The regulatory framing is important and management states it plainly elsewhere in the booklet: casinos cannot offer their products online, while 'online betting' operators — which is what playTSOGO and bet.co.za are, licensed as bookmakers — offer casino-style slots and tables at significantly lower tax rates. That arbitrage is why Tsogo's slot win is falling and simultaneously why its online NGR is rising; the taxation of online betting and casinos' ability to go online are 'subjects of discussion' with no resolution. Any convergence of online and land-based tax rates would be negative for the group's online margin but potentially positive for its casinos; any grant of online casino rights to land-based licensees would be clearly positive. Neither is in our numbers.

Stripping online out of the segment (our derivation; not disclosed) leaves bingo, HHR and sundry at roughly R236m (~$13m) of income, down ~22% from ~R302m, and roughly R23m (~$1.3m) of EBITDA, down from ~R35m — but up from ~R17m in H2 FY26. Galaxy Bingo remains structurally challenged by long-term leases, regulatory delays on site relocations and licence amendments, and illegal gambling sites; the model is moving to smaller, cheaper sites and loss-making sites are being closed as leases run out, which is what the income decline reflects. H1 FY26 carried R34m of impairments of bingo leasehold improvements; this period saw a R4m reversal on equipment sold, so the clean-up is largely done. The Historical Horse Racing terminal venture, run through associates under tote licences, is still 'in the start-up phase' — share of associate profit was R1m (~$0.06m) versus R3m — notwithstanding the May booklet's expectation that it would ramp in the second half of FY27; we carry nothing for it. Segment additions to non-current assets rose to R43m (~$2.5m) from R11m, consistent with the online platform and system build; gaming levies and VAT fell to R86m (~$4.9m) from R97m as bingo win declined.

highlights.text: Online betting is now a profit centre: NGR +43% to R193m (~$11m), adj. EBITDA R50m (~$2.8m) at a 26% margin (10% a year ago), profitable every month since August 2025 and running ~R8m/month — 3% of group EBITDA from a division that lost R15m in FY25.

Deleveraging target hit: net debt -R810m (~$46m) YoY and -R495m since March to R5.99bn (~$341m); covenant leverage 1.81x vs 2.01x a year ago against a <1.8x medium-term target and a 3.0x covenant; net finance costs -14% to R253m (~$14m).

Cash returns continue: R358m (~$20m) returned in the half (R291m dividends + R67m buying 10m shares at R6.70), interim DPS held at 15c (~0.9 USc), a further 4.7m shares bought post-period; shares in issue down to 965.6m from 1.04bn eighteen months ago, driving HEPS +7% to 79c (~4.5 USc).
KwaZulu-Natal reversed FY26's decline: EBITDA +3.7% to R423m (~$24m), margin +80bp to 39.0%, the portfolio's best — evidence the slot problem is not uniform across precincts.

LPMs defended margin at 28.5% (EBITDA R282m/~$16m, flat) while peer Sun Slots' EBITDA fell 8.1%; a newly constituted National Gambling Board (Oct 2026) is the first realistic path in a decade to lifting the R5/R500 limits set in 1996.
Hotels and non-gaming grew: rooms revenue +11.4% to R312m (~$18m), divisional revenue from contracts with customers +4.7% to R827m (~$47m), partially cushioning the gaming-win decline.
R70m (~$4.0m) of identified one-offs at EBITDA (strike R43m, once-off labour R16m, dividends R8m, VAT R3m): excluding them adj. EBITDA was ~R1.72bn (~$98m), flat YoY on our estimate.

lowlights.text: The core franchise is shrinking: net gaming win -3.4% to R4.45bn (~$253m), Casinos & Hotels EBITDA -6.9% to R1.41bn (~$80m) with margin -150bp to 35.4% (-160bp HoH); management and the impairment note both attribute it to slot win lost to online casino-style betting — a structural, tax-arbitrage-driven channel shift that is not reversing.

Gold Reef City is a running sore: Gauteng EBITDA -9.7% to R835m (~$48m); the strike cost ~R59m (~$3.4m) including once-off labour; Theme Park EBITDA -37%; the GRC licence was impaired R150m (~$8.5m) for the second consecutive period (R294m cumulative), with a further R273m (~$16m) at risk from a 1pp discount-rate move. Management says recovery 'is difficult'.

Post-period trading warning: 'October and November have been particularly tough trading months' — H2 is seasonally the stronger half, so the run-rate implies FY27 adj. EBITDA down mid-single digits and no earnings recovery before FY28.

Western Cape EBITDA -17% to R81m (~$4.6m), margin -360bp, and the ~R1.29bn (~$74m) Somerset West relocation that is supposed to fix it faces a High Court review (April 2027) brought by the ~82%-share incumbent — Tsogo is committing capital ahead of the ruling.

Earnings quality: headline earnings -2% to R757m (~$43m), attributable profit -7% to R630m (~$36m), IFRS operating profit -9% to R1.15bn (~$66m); all per-share growth is buyback-driven, and 54%-holder HCI's stake creeps higher with every repurchase.

Online disclosure is inadequate for the valuation weight being placed on it: no handle, actives, ARPU, promo intensity, product mix or marketing spend; sequential NGR growth slowed to +8% from +32%; at R193m of half-year NGR the business is ~one-sixth of SunBet and the earlier 'invest aggressively / new platform' language has been dropped.

Refinancing and rate risk: R4.45bn (~$254m) matures in calendar 2027 (Feb/May/Aug/Nov) after +50bp of SARB hikes; current liabilities (R4.49bn) exceed current assets (R1.02bn) pending completion; employee costs rose 2.6% to R1.0bn (~$57m, 18.4% of income, +90bp) on a -2% top line.

Regulatory overhang widening, not narrowing: proposed ban on casino smoking areas, provincial attempts to raise casino taxes, unresolved online tax regime and online rights for casinos, the Gambling Amendment Bill's system-cost burden, and the Eastern Cape LPM licence rebid (March 2027).

forecast.intro: Tsogo Sun issues no earnings guidance, so the 'bridge' is between the quantified guideposts in the May 2026 FY26 release and this booklet. Three moved: FY27 capex was trimmed to ~R1.1bn (~$63m) from R1.2bn (the GRC refurbishment, Theme Park 5D cinema, IT, gaming equipment and Somerset West all sit inside it, with R1bn contracted); the medium-term leverage target of <1.8x was 'effectively achieved' at 1.81x versus 1.92x in March; and the Somerset West relocation timeline compressed to ~18 months from ~24, with the cost estimate (~R1.29bn/~$74m from the Nov-25 booklet) not updated. The fourth change is qualitative and negative: the conclusion still promises 'resilient headline earnings per share' but the Casinos & Hotels commentary adds that October and November were 'particularly tough', which is the division — slots in Gauteng and the Western Cape — that drove the H1 shortfall. Online and LPMs are not the problem; the refinancing of R4.45bn (~$254m) of 2027 maturities is 'in advanced stages' and the 2027 RCF can be called on 13 months' notice.

forecast.view: Our model (estimates, not company guidance) takes management at its word on October/November and assumes no festive-season rescue. For H2 FY27 we pencil income of ~R5.43bn (~$310m), -2.5% YoY against H2 FY26's R5.57bn, and adj. EBITDA of ~R1.63bn (~$93m) at a ~30.0% margin (-140bp YoY; H2 FY26 was 31.4%), which gives **FY27 income ~R10.86bn (~$619m), -2.4%, and adj. EBITDA ~R3.28bn (~$187m), -5.4%, at a 30.2% margin (-90bp)**. By division that is Casinos & Hotels ~R2.80bn (-7%), LPMs ~R0.56bn (flat), Other gaming & betting ~R0.15bn (+45%, online ~R105m), Corporate ~-R0.23bn. Below the line, net finance costs ex-leases of ~R500m (~$28m) for the year (R253m in H1, ~R250m in H2 as lower debt is offset by the +50bp SARB hikes and any refinancing spread), D&A ~R660m and a ~28% tax rate give **FY27 headline earnings of ~R1.50–1.53bn (~$86–87m), -3% to -4%, and HEPS of ~157–160c (~9.0–9.1 USc), +3% to +5%** on ~958m weighted shares — i.e. the buyback continues to do the work, and the FY26 booklet's '8% HEPS growth' cadence is not repeatable without further repurchases. **Leverage keeps falling**: H2 pre-dividend operating cash flow of ~R1.1bn less ~R750m capex, ~R165m of dividends (interim + NCI), ~R50m of buybacks, plus ~R110m of land and listed-share proceeds, takes net debt to ~R5.7–5.8bn (~$325–330m) at March 2027 and covenant leverage to ~1.75x — comfortably inside target, before Somerset West spend lifts FY28 capex back toward R1.2–1.3bn. We assume the final dividend is held at 30c for a **45c (~2.6 USc) FY27 total, ~R435m (~$25m)**, and a similar ~R0.1–0.2bn of buybacks. Risks to the EBITDA line are skewed to the downside (December trading, GRC recovery, smoking-area legislation, provincial tax); the upside swing factors — LPM limit adjustment, online rights for casinos, a favourable court outcome in April — are regulatory, binary and not in our numbers. The equity remains a cash-yield-plus-deleveraging story priced at ~4.5x trailing HEPS; the H2 trading warning and the 2027 refinancing terms are what will move it near term.
watch: December/January festive trading at Montecasino, Gold Reef City (post-refurbishment) and Suncoast: does the Oct/Nov slot run-rate (our assumption: net gaming win -3% to -4%) persist into Q4 FY27, and is the GRC licence impaired again at March 2027 (R273m sensitivity to +1pp discount rate)?
Refinancing terms for the R4.45bn (~$254m) of 2027 maturities — spread, tenor and whether the group terms out the R1.5bn November 2027 RCF; the going-concern note relies on completion.

Western Cape High Court review of the Somerset West relocation (hearing April 2027): an adverse ruling strands early spend and leaves the Caledon problem unsolved; a favourable one commits ~R1.29bn (~$74m) of capex into FY28–29.

Online betting: whether NGR growth re-accelerates from +8% HoH, any first disclosure of actives/handle/marketing, and the direction of online-betting tax reform and casino online rights — both of which cut across Tsogo's land-based and online economics in opposite directions.

Regulatory calendar: tobacco/smoking-area legislation; provincial casino tax proposals; the new NGB's stance on LPM bet/payout limits and second-phase roll-outs; Eastern Cape LPM licence rebid (expires March 2027); the parked National Gambling Amendment Bill.

Capital allocation and control: buyback cadence (4.7m shares post-period at R6.70) versus HCI's 54% and rising indirect stake; proceeds from the R48m land sale and R65m listed shares; final dividend decision in May 2027.
